- **Three-field rotation** [`three_field_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/three_field_system.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Italy sows winter grain and fallows every other year; dry summers make a spring-sown third field unreliable outside the Po plain. The gain lies north of the Alps.
- **Legumes and green manure** [`legumes_green_manure`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/legumes_green_manure.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Cato lists lupins, beans and vetch as crops that manure the land, and good farmers plough lupins in. Absentee owners with slave gangs often skip it. Local: Cato, De agri cultura 37; Mago's farming books (Latin translation by D. Silanus).
- **Four-course rotation with clover and turnips** [`crop_rotation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crop_rotation.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Grain after beans is practised, but fallow remains the rule and fodder is scarce. Lucerne (medica) and turnips are grown; red clover as a sown field crop is not.
- **Manure, compost and night soil** [`manure_compost_night_soil`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/manure_compost_night_soil.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Dung heaps and pigeon dung are prized (Cato). The city's excrement mostly goes down the sewers into the Tiber; only market gardens near the walls buy it. Local: market gardens around the city walls; Cato, De agri cultura.
- **Liming and marling of sour soils** [`liming_marling`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/liming_marling.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept low. Varro saw Gauls near the Rhine dress fields with dug white earth. Italian soils on limestone and volcanic ash seldom need it. Local: Marcus Terentius Varro. Elsewhere: Transalpine Gaul, marling.
- **Mineral fertiliser (guano, phosphate, potash, nitrate)** [`mineral_fertiliser`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mineral_fertiliser.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Wood ash is used on fields. Bone meal and ash are within reach; guano, mined phosphate and potash are not. The idea that plants eat dissolved minerals contradicts Aristotle.
- **Terracing and soil conservation** [`terracing_soil_conservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/terracing_soil_conservation.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Hillside vines and olives stand on dry-stone terraces. Grazing and felling strip the Apennine slopes, and the Tiber silts and floods. Nobody connects the two.
- **Heavy mouldboard plough** [`heavy_plough`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/heavy_plough.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. The Italian ard scratches light soil crosswise and suits it. A wheeled plough with coulter and mouldboard pays only on heavy wet land: the Po plain and Gaul. Elsewhere: Han China, cast-iron shares and mouldboards.
- **Horse collar and breast-strap harness** [`horse_collar_harness`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/horse_collar_harness.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Oxen plough and haul under the yoke, mules carry and draw carts; horses are for war and racing. A saddler can make a padded collar in days. Elsewhere: Han China, breast-strap harness.
- **Seed drill** [`seed_drill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/seed_drill.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Seed is broadcast by hand and ploughed in. Slave labour is cheap; saved seed grain is the argument, since a large share of every wheat crop goes back as seed. Elsewhere: Han China, multi-tube seed drill; Mesopotamia, plough with seed funnel.
- **Scythe and grain cradle** [`scythe_cradle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scythe_cradle.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Hay is mown with a short scythe; grain is cut with the sickle, often high on the stalk. A long scythe with a cradle is smith's and carpenter's work. Elsewhere: Gaul, longer scythes.
- **Mechanical reaper and threshing machine** [`reaper_thresher`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/reaper_thresher.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Grain is trodden out by animals or a threshing sledge (tribulum) and winnowed in the wind. Harvest gangs of slaves and hired men make owners indifferent to machines. Elsewhere: Han China, rotary winnowing fan.
- **Selective breeding of plants and animals** [`selective_breeding`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/selective_breeding.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Stock owners choose rams, bulls and stallions by looks and pedigree, and prize Reate donkeys. Seed corn is picked from the best ears. No records, no progeny testing. Local: Marcus Terentius Varro (stock farms at Reate); mule and donkey breeders of Reate.
- **Grafting of fruit trees and vines** [`grafting_fruit_trees`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grafting_fruit_trees.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Cato describes cleft and bud grafting step by step. Lucullus brought the cherry from Pontus a generation ago; new fruits are a nobleman's hobby. Local: Cato, De agri cultura 40-42; gardens of Lucullus on the Pincian.
- **Irrigation and water lifting (canal, qanat, shaduf, noria)** [`irrigation_water_lifting`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/irrigation_water_lifting.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Gardens are watered from channels and by the well sweep; Lucretius mentions river-turned wheels with scoops. Archimedes' screw drains Spanish mines. Field crops rely on winter rain. Elsewhere: Egypt, screw, ox-driven wheel and shaduf.
- **Wet rice (paddy) cultivation** [`wet_rice_cultivation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/wet_rice_cultivation.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Rice is known from Greek accounts of India and as an imported invalid's food. Seed would have to come from the East; the Po marshes would suit it. Elsewhere: India; China.
- **Polders – land reclamation with dikes and wind pumps** [`windmill_drainage_land_reclamation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/windmill_drainage_land_reclamation.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Romans drain by gravity with channels and tunnels (Alban Lake emissary, Etruscan cuniculi). Caesar will plan to drain the Pomptine marshes and Fucine Lake (45–44 BC). Windmills are unknown. Local: Pomptine marshes; Fucine Lake; emissary of the Alban Lake.
- **Fish ponds and carp polyculture** [`aquaculture_fish_ponds`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/aquaculture_fish_ponds.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Sea-water fish ponds are a rich man's craze and Lucrine oysters a business since Sergius Orata. Hirrius lends Caesar thousands of morays, by weight, for the triumph banquets. Pure luxury. Local: Gaius Hirrius; oyster beds of the Lucrine Lake; villa fish ponds on the Bay of Naples.

- **Food preservation (salting, drying, smoking, pickling)** [`food_preservation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/food_preservation.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Salted fish and fish sauce (garum) from Spain and the Black Sea, Cato's salted hams, dried figs, raisins, olives in brine, smoked cheese, fruit in honey or boiled must. Local: Cato, De agri cultura 162 (salting hams); fish-sauce importers at Puteoli and Ostia.
- **Canning (heat-preserving in sealed containers)** [`canning`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/canning.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium. Small jars, cork, pitch and wax exist; glass jars are few and tinplate is absent. Boiling sealed pottery is workable. Under-heated meat or beans in a sealed jar can kill.
- **Pasteurisation** [`pasteurisation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pasteurisation.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Wine often turns to vinegar; growers answer with pitch, resin, salt water and boiled must. Gently heating sealed jars fits their habits. Milk is drunk fresh or made into cheese. Local: wine growers of Latium and Campania.
- **Grain storage and protection from pests and ergot** [`grain_storage_pest_control`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/grain_storage_pest_control.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. State and private warehouses hold the dole grain; floors are plastered with olive lees against weevils (Cato 92). Losses to damp, heating, weevils and rats are large. Rye is rare. Local: warehouses of the Sulpicii Galbae (later Horrea Galbana) and the Tiber wharves below the Aventine; Puteoli (grain ships unload); aediles in charge of the grain supply. Elsewhere: Han China, 'ever-normal granary' price buffer (54 BC); Egypt, royal granaries at Alexandria.
- **Sea fisheries – stockfish, salt cod and cured herring** [`sea_fisheries_salt_cod`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sea_fisheries_salt_cod.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept medium. - **Sugar from cane and from beet** [`sugar_cane_beet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sugar_cane_beet.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept high. Honey and boiled must are the sweeteners. Greeks report an Indian reed giving honey without bees. Cane cuttings are a sea voyage beyond Egypt; garden beet holds too little sugar. - **Sericulture (silk raising)** [`sericulture`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sericulture.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept high. Silk is the costliest cloth; awnings at Caesar's games are said to be of it. People think it grows on trees. Silkworm eggs and white mulberry exist only in China. Elsewhere: Han China; Cos, wild silk woven into thin cloth.
- **Movable-frame beehive** [`beekeeping_movable_frame`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/beekeeping_movable_frame.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept medium.
